summary: Three independent attempts to fix the Part-2 ShareRobot direction problem, all falsified the duplicated-history hypothesis as the sole cause.

attempt_2_H3_real_frames_noisy_depth.result: zero motion predicted (model likely distrusted an implausible 3D history)

attempt_3_H3_real_frames_consistent_dept.depth: single t0 depth map reused for all 3 frames (physically consistent)
attempt_3_H3_real_frames_consistent_dept.note: predicted direction is close to OPPOSITE the real history direction it was just given

attempt_4_H3_calibrated_REAL_ground_trut.depth: NOT estimated: the exact source BridgeData V2 episode was identified (ShareRobot is a curated subset of several Open-X-Embodiment datasets, 'bridge' among them; matched via instruction-text search in bridge_orig_lerobot's meta/tasks.jsonl, confirmed with a pixel-identical frame-0 match: bridge_orig_lerobot episode_index 45932, task_index 17429). points_3d_history uses the REAL measured 6-DOF WidowX end-effector pose for the anchor point, transformed into camera frame via our own solvePnP-estimated extrinsics (fit on the 8 pre-grasp frames only, where our 2D gripper tracker and the robot's end-effector are the same physical point; mean reprojection error 12.0px on a 640x480 image, i.e. ~2%).
attempt_4_H3_calibrated_REAL_ground_trut.result: ZERO motion predicted (the model's output text is a flat, frame-to-frame-IDENTICAL relative-offset pattern; the anchor's predicted path start == end)
attempt_4_H3_calibrated_REAL_ground_trut.note: This is the strongest version of the experiment: real, non-duplicated, non-estimated history AND a real (not self-reconstructed) ground-truth future to compare against. The model still fails -- not with a wrong direction this time, but with no predicted motion at all, on an input whose real displacement is not small (0.13m history, 0.10m future).

conclusion: Across 4 independently-constructed real (non-duplicated) history inputs -- including, in the final attempt, REAL measured 3D ground truth (not estimated depth) traced back to the original BridgeData V2 episode and a self-calibrated camera (not an assumed FOV alone) -- the model never produces a correct, confident future-motion prediction for this ShareRobot/tabletop-manipulation episode: wrong direction in 3 attempts (cosine -0.60 to -0.62, one case exactly opposite its own input history at -0.97), and zero motion in the 4th despite a clean, well-grounded, genuinely non-trivial-displacement input. Ruling out, in order: duplicated history (attempts 2-4 all used real history), depth-estimation noise (attempt 3 fixed depth consistency, still wrong; attempt 4 removed depth estimation entirely, still fails), and now also the quality/correctness of the 3D input itself (attempt 4's input is about as clean as this machine can produce without the original dataset's own camera calibration file, which doesn't appear to be published). This is a genuine, well-characterized model limitation on out-of-domain (tabletop robot manipulation) inputs, not an artifact of our data pipeline -- the kind of result that would need retraining or fine-tuning on robot-manipulation data to fix, not more careful input construction.
